name: Ironband's Excavation Site
summary: In southeastern Loch Modan, troggs have driven the miners from Ironband's Excavation Site. The dig lies south of the Loch and southwest of Farstrider Lodge.

sections.title: Unearthing the Past
sections.body: Prospector Ironband began the dig to seek the dwarves’ ancient Titan origins. Then the miners disturbed an unusually fierce and large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth and drove the miners back. Now they camp among scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics.

sections.title: Ruins in the Red Earth
sections.body: Troggs hold the site while surviving prospectors wait at its perimeter. Like archaeological efforts in the Badlands, Wetlands, and Uldaman, this dig is caught in danger. The prospectors hope to reclaim their stolen gear and guard exposed artifacts from the ravenous troggs. Strange ancient statues remain among those artifacts, left by long-forgotten builders.

faq.q: Where is Ironband's Excavation Site located?
faq.answer: Ironband's Excavation Site lies in southeastern Loch Modan, south of the Loch and southwest of Farstrider Lodge.
Prospector Ironband is an archaeologist and explorer leading the Explorers' League excavation. He is trying to salvage artifacts and drive back the local troggs.

faq.q: Why is the excavation site overrun with troggs?
faq.answer: Miners dug deeper into Loch Modan and broke into underground pockets inhabited by a large, aggressive breed of troggs. The troggs overwhelmed the workers and seized the site.

faq.q: What were the dwarves hoping to find here?
faq.answer: The dwarves hoped to find ancient Titan relics and stone ruins that could shed light on their race's ancestral origins.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you know that losing this dig is a stinging setback for the Explorers' League. Recovering ancient relics here matters to understanding dwarven heritage.
As a miner, you can see how dwarves use heavy extraction techniques in the quarry and open pits. Trogg hostility makes prospecting hazardous.
